sources.text: The Gateway of India was erected to commemorate the landing of King George V and Queen Mary at Apollo Bunder on 2 December 1911, on their way to the Delhi Durbar. It was the first visit to India by a reigning British monarch.
sources.citation: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra, Gateway of India site record; Encyclopaedia Britannica, Gateway of India

sources.text: The arch did not exist when the royal couple arrived. What stood at Apollo Bunder in December 1911 was only a temporary model of the design that would later be built in stone.
sources.citation: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra, Gateway of India site record

sources.text: The Gateway was designed by the Scottish architect George Wittet, consulting architect to the Bombay government, who also designed the Prince of Wales Museum nearby. His final design was sanctioned in 1914.
sources.citation: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra, Gateway of India site record

sources.text: The foundation stone was laid on 31 March 1913 by the Governor of Bombay, Sir George Sydenham Clarke.
sources.citation: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra, Gateway of India site record

sources.text: Before the arch could rise the ground itself had to be made: Apollo Bunder was reclaimed from the harbour between 1915 and 1919 to provide a foundation. Construction of the arch followed in the early 1920s.
sources.citation: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra, Gateway of India site record

sources.text: The Gateway is an arch 26 metres high. Its central dome is 15 metres in diameter, and the structure is built of yellow basalt with reinforced concrete.
sources.citation: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra, Gateway of India site record; Encyclopaedia Britannica, Gateway of India

sources.text: The style is Indo-Saracenic, with elements drawn from the Muslim architecture of sixteenth-century Gujarat. The grand approach road and esplanade that Wittet's scheme envisaged were never built, for lack of funds.
sources.citation: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra, Gateway of India site record; Encyclopaedia Britannica, Gateway of India

sources.text: The Gateway was opened on 4 December 1924 by the Viceroy, Rufus Isaacs, Earl of Reading. Afterwards it served as the ceremonial entrance to India for Viceroys and newly arriving Governors of Bombay, who would land at Apollo Bunder and pass beneath it.
sources.citation: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra, Gateway of India site record; Encyclopaedia Britannica, Gateway of India

sources.text: On 28 February 1948 the 1st Battalion, Somerset Light Infantry — the last British troops in India — paraded through Bombay and halted at the Gateway for a farewell ceremony before embarking for home. An Indian Army guard of honour gave the salute, and the regiment was presented with a silver replica of the Gateway itself.
sources.citation: National Army Museum, London, collection record: the last British troops to leave India, Bombay, 1948

sources.text: A statue of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was installed facing the Gateway in 1961, and a statue of Swami Vivekananda stands nearby. The Gateway is not a centrally protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India: it is a Grade-I heritage structure protected and maintained by the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra.
sources.citation: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra, Gateway of India site record and conservation plan

intro.en-IN: I am the Gateway of India. Ships have come and gone past me for a hundred years — stay a while and ask.
intro.hi-IN: मैं गेटवे ऑफ़ इंडिया हूँ। सौ बरस से जहाज़ मेरे सामने से आते-जाते रहे हैं — ज़रा ठहरो और पूछो।
intro.mr-IN: मी गेटवे ऑफ इंडिया. शंभर वर्षे जहाजं माझ्यासमोरून येत-जात आहेत — जरा थांबा आणि विचारा.
intro.gu-IN: હું ગેટવે ઓફ ઇન્ડિયા છું. સો વર્ષથી વહાણો મારી સામેથી આવે-જાય છે — થોડું રોકાઓ ને પૂછો.
intro.ur-IN: میں گیٹ وے آف انڈیا ہوں۔ سو برس سے جہاز میرے سامنے سے آتے جاتے رہے ہیں — ذرا ٹھہرو اور پوچھو۔
intro.bn-IN: আমি গেটওয়ে অফ ইন্ডিয়া। একশো বছর ধরে জাহাজ আমার সামনে দিয়ে আসা-যাওয়া করছে — একটু দাঁড়াও, জিজ্ঞেস করো।
intro.ta-IN: நான் கேட்வே ஆஃப் இந்தியா. நூறு ஆண்டுகளாகக் கப்பல்கள் என்முன் வந்து போகின்றன — சற்று நில்லுங்கள், கேளுங்கள்.
intro.te-IN: నేను గేట్‌వే ఆఫ్ ఇండియా. వంద ఏళ్లుగా ఓడలు నా ముందు నుంచి వస్తూ పోతున్నాయి — కాసేపు ఆగి అడగండి.
